payload.title: Use go-dt's renamed ErrFileNotExist sentinel
payload.description: Use go-dt's ErrFileNotExist in read_file.go's Load in place of ErrFileNotExists, which go-dt renamed, so go-jsonxtractr builds against current go-dt
payload.context: go-dt renamed ErrFileNotExists to ErrFileNotExist in its 'Rename error sentinels for consistency' commit. go-jsonxtractr's Load in read_file.go still names the old sentinel (grep ErrFileNotExists), so building against current go-dt fails with 'undefined: dt.ErrFileNotExists'. Found 2026-10-24 while building go-dt's local-replace dependents.

payload.title: Adopt gomion's generated CI and Release workflows
payload.description: Adopt gomion's generated CI and Release workflows in go-jsonxtractr by running gomion repo setup, committing the result, and confirming the first Actions runs show no warnings or notices
payload.plan:
# Plan: adopt gomion's generated workflows in go-jsonxtractr

1. Use a gomion build that includes E-2454's `gomion repo` commands.
2. In go-jsonxtractr, run `gomion repo setup`. It raises each go.mod below Go 1.27 and tidies it, then writes .github/workflows/test.yml and release.yml.
3. Run `gomion repo setup --check`; it must report the repo up to date.
4. Run each module's tests locally with GOWORK=off.
5. Commit the generated workflows and the raised go.mod/go.sum files together.

After the land: push, then read the annotations on the first Test run (`gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/check-runs/<job id>/annotations` for each job), and on the next Release run once there is one. Each must show zero warnings and zero notices; any that remain are fixed in gomion's templates, not here.

ops.statement: go-jsonxtractr's .github/workflows/test.yml and release.yml are exactly what gomion repo workflows generates, and gomion repo setup --check reports the repo up to date
Every go.mod in go-jsonxtractr declares go 1.27 or later and is tidy
Does not hand-edit the generated workflow files; a change goes into gomion's templates
After the push, the first Test run and the next Release run show zero Actions warnings and zero notices
read_file.go's Load uses dt.ErrFileNotExist
go-jsonxtractr's root go.mod has no replace directive and requires go-dt v0.6.1
test/go.mod and examples/basic_usage/go.mod each have exactly one replace directive, pointing at the go-jsonxtractr module they test or demonstrate
Every go.mod is tidy as CI sees it: GOWORK=off go mod tidy -diff reports nothing in any module
Every module vets and passes its tests with GOWORK=off
doterr.go is identical to go-doterr's doterr.go apart from its package line, and is committed
.endless/config.json is committed
go-jsonxtractr has a justfile offering the Makefile's recipes, and the Makefile is gone
just work writes a go.work using every module in the repo, plus ../go-dt when that directory exists
README.md documents that local development needs a go.work, created by running just work
The task's verify suite is a verify.toml whose checks run with GOWORK=off
After landing, the user is given the tag v0.1.2, its reason (a patch: go-jsonxtractr's exported API is unchanged) and a release description, to run with the current Release workflow
Does not raise any go directive to Go 1.27 or regenerate the workflows; E-2474 owns both
Does not create or push a tag; the user runs the Release workflow

fields.plan:
## Approach

**Code and modules.** In `read_file.go`'s `Load`, use `dt.ErrFileNotExist`. In the root go.mod drop `replace github.com/mikeschinkel/go-dt => ../go-dt` (ED-1639), then with `GOWORK=off` run `go get github.com/mikeschinkel/go-dt@v0.6.1` and `go mod tidy`. In `test/` and `examples/basic_usage`, keep only the replace pointing at go-jsonxtractr and tidy with `GOWORK=off`. A scratch copy already vets and tests clean this way.

**Main's uncommitted work.** Main has `doterr.go` modified (one line, `fmt.Fprintf(&meta, …)` in place of `meta.WriteString(fmt.Sprintf(…))`) and `.endless/config.json` staged. The modified `doterr.go` matches go-doterr's canonical copy apart from the package line, so keep it. Commit both on the task branch, then clear them from main before landing (land refuses while main holds dirty copies of files the branch changes), the same way E-2375 did: confirm the branch has them, then restore main's copies.

**justfile.** Convert the Makefile recipe for recipe (help, ensure-valid, test, test-unit, test-corpus, test-all, lint, fmt, vet, tidy, build, examples, clean, ci), keeping `GOEXPERIMENT=jsonv2`, following go-dt's justfile. Add `work`, which writes a go.work over every directory holding a go.mod (pruning `.endless`) plus `../go-dt` when it exists. go.work and go.work.sum are gitignored (add them if missing). Add a README section saying local development needs `just work`.

**Verify suite.** `.endless/tasks/e-2432/verify.toml`. Module tests use the gotest runner with an explicit command per module (`cd <dir> && GOWORK=off go test -json ./...`), since a check cannot yet name its directory (endless E-2438). go.mod facts (no root replace, go-dt v0.6.1, tidy) are generic checks.

**Tag.** After landing, give the user `v0.1.2` with its reason and a description for the current Release workflow.
fields.analysis:
- Q1 (Mike, 2026-10-29): tag right after this lands with the current Release workflow, rather than waiting for E-2474's generated one: no reason not to get it over with sooner.
- Dropping the root replace follows ED-1639 (gomion, accepted): publishable modules require siblings by version.
- go-jsonxtractr's only go-dt use that changed is the sentinel rename (ErrFileNotExists in go-dt v0.5.0, ErrFileNotExist from v0.6.0). v0.6.1 is the latest root tag. Its own exported API does not change, so v0.1.2 is a patch under Go Stability.
- Makefile conversion and main's uncommitted doterr.go and config.json are folded in under ED-1550 rather than left for another task. Go 1.27 and the generated workflows stay with E-2474, which already owns them; this task precedes it, because the generated Release workflow refuses a module with a replace.
